title: Doctor timeout can outlive its own deadline: failed kill leaves an unbounded wait, and both results are discarded
outcome:
On expiry the enablement/verify doctor path does `let _ = child.kill(); let _ = child.wait();` and discards both results, then returns "Engram doctor exceeded the N second enablement deadline". Two consequences, and the second is worse than a silent error.

1. A FAILED KILL IS INVISIBLE. Nothing in the response, the state, or any log records that the doctor was not actually terminated. The caller is told the deadline was enforced; whether the process died is unknown to everyone.

2. THE DEADLINE DOES NOT BOUND THE REQUEST. If `kill()` fails, `wait()` blocks until the child exits on its own. The polling loop is bounded; the reap after it is not. So the message can promise "exceeded the 300 second deadline" while the HTTP call returns much later - or, against a genuinely hung doctor, never. The enable/verify call runs through run_blocking_api, so a blocking worker thread is held for that whole time. This is the shape the deadline exists to prevent, surviving inside the code that enforces it.

WHY IT IS FILED SEPARATELY: the deadline-value fix deliberately did not touch it. Making the reap observable changes the function's contract, and testing it with a process scan would be a non-discriminating instrument. Named here so the gap is carried explicitly instead of quietly.

SCOPE NOTE, so this does not grow into process-tree management: `kill()` here terminates the direct child only. Engram::Advisor searched the Engram sources for Command::new/process::Command/.spawn and found no subprocess spawning by the doctor - a bounded source review, not a runtime observation of the tree. So a tree kill is probably unnecessary for this path. By contrast the control-process path already uses EngramProcessTree::terminate and has a test named real_process_timeout_kills_the_entire_control_process_tree; the asymmetry is deliberate to note, not automatically a defect.

MINIMUM SHAPE IF TAKEN UP: bound the post-kill wait (or use a try_wait loop with its own small budget) so the expiry path cannot outlive its own deadline, and surface a failed kill rather than discarding it. Neither requires new telemetry or UI.
disposal_reason: Backlog triage w-930e4d333f07 (Architect1 batch 1b, spot-checked by Termal::Fable2): CLOSE-DONE. Doctor execution is bounded, landed in 0e7ab55 (ancestor of master f7db2c58). Closed by evidence.
